descriptionChirho: Plural noun וָוִים referring to the hooks or pegs used in the construction of the tabernacle, specifically the metal hooks on the pillars of the court and the holy place from which curtains were hung. All 13 occurrences appear in Exodus 26-38 describing tabernacle construction. The construct form ('hooks of') and suffixed form ('their hooks') represent the same architectural element in different possessive constructions. Translated as English 'hooks,' Spanish 'ganchos,' Hindi 'huk' (हुक), Arabic 'khatatif' (خَطَاطِيفُ), Korean 'geolgori' (걸고리), Swahili 'kulabu.' No semantic distinction exists between construct and pronominal-suffix forms.
